findings.issue: After Thread.sleep(1100) the demote-after-disable assertion is isGreaterThanOrEqualTo(first). That still passes if the second write never advances the cutoff, so the end-to-end test does not prove that the cutoff moves forward. AccessTokenDenyStoreTest.higherCutoffAdvances does cover advancing at the unit level.
findings.fix: Assert cutoff() isGreaterThan(first). The 1.1 s sleep already guarantees a later epoch second.

findings.issue: The clock is reset with advanceBy at the end of tests, but JUnit creates a new test instance (and a new FixedTimeProvider) per method, so the resets do nothing and suggest shared state that does not exist.
verify(denyStore, never()).revokeIssuedUpTo(...) repeats the check that verifyNoInteractions(denyStore) already makes.

The else branch of afterCommit() runs the action immediately when no synchronization is active. Both callers are @Transactional, so this branch cannot be reached; if it ever were, it would quietly skip the after-commit guarantee.
findings.fix: Optional: keep it, as it matches the WarehouseService/AuditPublisher pattern, or document that the branch is unreachable.

findings.issue: The stored value is parsed in two places: Long.valueOf in AccessTokenDenyStore.cutoffOf and Long::parseLong in DenyListReactiveJwtDecoder. The rest of the format (key and comparison) is already shared.
findings.fix: Optional: add a parseCutoff(String) helper to AccessTokenDenyList so the value format is defined once.

summary: The change is correct and minimal, and it meets all 7 CTO conditions. (1) The Lua script coerces both values with tonumber, the missing-key case becomes 0, and math.max makes the write forward-only. The real-Redis test shows a lower second write leaves the stored value at 1800000000. (2) The gateway throws BadJwtException (both the revoked and null-sub paths). Auth returns OAuth2TokenValidatorResult.failure, which NimbusJwtDecoder raises as JwtValidationException, a BadJwtException subtype. G2 asserts a 401 application/problem+json body with code UNAUTHENTICATED, and the auth MockMvc test asserts 401 AUTH_TOKEN_INVALID. (3) A null or blank sub is rejected before any key is built: the gateway throws BadJwtException, auth returns a NO_SUBJECT failure, and AccessTokenDenyList.key throws. Tests prove Redis is never touched in that case. (4) auth now sets spring.data.redis.timeout to 500ms and the gateway already had 500ms. Both check points fail open with a WARN and a *.access_deny.check.unavailable counter, and parse errors also fail open. In the gateway, onErrorResume sits before the revoked flatMap, so a BadJwtException is never swallowed. (5) The TTL is accessTokenTtl + 60 s = 660 s, asserted to be within [600, 660]. The write is registered through TransactionSynchronization.afterCommit on the outer transaction (after the REQUIRES_NEW revokeAllSessions returns), so a rollback or refusal writes nothing and enable never deletes the key; all of this is tested. iat is compared in whole seconds (getEpochSecond <=), and a token issued in the same second as the cutoff is treated as revoked, which is tested. On coverage: the gateway has a single SecurityWebFilterChain, and its bearer decoding runs on permitAll paths too. auth has a single JwtDecoder; the only other Nimbus parse, at AuthController:316, reads a token it just issued and is not an acceptance point. Downstream replay is accepted residual risk B-8 and is recorded in ADR 0005. Each SecurityConfig change is limited to the decoder bean wiring. The common-security addition is a new, framework-free final class and does not change existing types. Reuse is appropriate: the after-commit pattern, the fail-open pattern from RateLimitWebFilter, AuthMetrics and the shared lib. No existing deny-list or JDK/Spring facility is duplicated. The tests would fail if the code broke, apart from one weak end-to-end assertion (minor). No blocker or major findings.
